name: Maher 2004
question: How do abdominal sacral colpopexy and vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy compare for vaginal vault prolapse?

design.population: Ninety-five women with vaginal vault prolapse were randomized.

verdictNote: Success rates did not differ significantly; a prespecified comparative threshold was unavailable.
takeaway: Among women with vaginal vault prolapse, abdominal sacral colpopexy and vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy did not differ significantly in reported subjective or objective success at approximately two years; the abdominal route had longer operating time, slower return to daily activities, and greater cost.

reports.label: Primary report
reports.citation: Maher CF, Qatawneh AM, Dwyer PL, et al. "Abdominal sacral colpopexy or vaginal sacrospinous colpopexy for vaginal vault prolapse: a prospective randomized study." *Am J Obstet Gynecol.* 2004;190(1):20-26. doi:10.1016/j.ajog.2003.08.031

results.note: The abstract does not give assessed denominators or a prespecified comparative threshold.
The abstract does not define objective success, give assessed denominators, or specify a comparative threshold.
The abstract reports significant improvement after both operations without a between-group estimate.

delivery.label: Operating time, return to daily activities, and cost
delivery.value: The abdominal route had longer operating time, slower return to daily activities, and greater cost than the vaginal route (P<0.01 for the reported comparison).
